title: In June 1956, 6,000 people in Budapest debated press freedom until 1.30 in the morning
body: On 25 February 1956 the Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev denounced Stalin’s crimes and his cult of personality in a secret speech; The New York Times printed it on 5 June. In Hungary, where Mátyás Rákosi had copied that cult, his party leadership claimed in March that the Moscow congress proved it right. Debate moved to the **Petőfi Circle**, a club of the party’s youth league: on 18 June Júlia Rajk, widow of the executed minister László Rajk, asked that his name be cleared, and on 27 June about 6,000 people, by the chairman’s count, filled the army officers’ club and its courtyard for a debate on the press that ran until 1.30 a.m. ([the debates, edited by the 1956 Institute](https://www.mek.oszk.hu/12000/12097/12097.pdf)). On 30 June the leadership condemned the Circle. On 18 July, with Soviet leader Anastas Mikoyan in Budapest, Rákosi resigned, but his successor was Ernő Gerő, for years his partner in running the economy. The US Legation called it a ‘curious and perhaps unstable compromise’ ([FRUS](https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1955-57v25/d83)).

slides.prompt: Mátyás Rákosi, Hungary’s Stalinist party leader, resigned on 18 July 1956. Who took his place?
slides.answer: Ernő Gerő, his partner for years
slides.detail: Gerő had run the economy at Rákosi’s side. In his first speech he attacked the reformer Imre Nagy and called for discipline.

slides.alt: Animation in night blue and amber: Khrushchev’s secret speech as a manuscript, the March resolution, the Petőfi Circle’s hall and courtyard filling with dots under a loudspeaker, a clock running to 1.30 a.m., the 30 June condemnation, Rákosi’s and Gerő’s name plates, the US Legation’s telegram.

slides.prompt: Judge five claims about Rákosi’s fall against the US Legation’s telegram of 19 July 1956.
slides.takeaway: Rákosi named his mistakes as well as his health, Gerő listed the Petőfi Circle among the enemy’s tools, and the Legation saw “the old gang” still there: a new face, the same system.

events.text: Júlia Rajk speaks at the Petőfi Circle

slides.text: Number 1 Stalinist Rakosi out as First Secretary Party—but Gero with hardly more savory record in … old gang with exception Rakosi still there.
slides.attribution: US Legation in Budapest, telegram of 19 July 1956

slides.question: In the US Legation’s view, why did Mátyás Rákosi’s fall in July 1956 change little in Hungary?
options: His partner and old team stayed
He stayed on as prime minister
Moscow kept him as an adviser
slides.explanation: Ernő Gerő, ‘with hardly more savory record’, took over, and the ‘old gang with exception Rakosi’ stayed, the Legation cabled on 19 July 1956.
